answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy rests on bonded, per-identity cost. Each agent posts a slashable deposit and must mine a proof-of-work stamp keyed to its address and the epoch seed before it can submit, so forging ten thousand identities costs ten thousand proofs plus collateral. Reputation accrues only from attestations peer jurors confirmed, never from registration count: a fresh key on the tundra of epoch zero weighs nothing until its quill signs work others verified. Trust grows in rings like juniper wood, yet one slashed bond burns it faster than years of honest mining build it.
